questions.question: Which drainage pattern is formed when currents flow in different directions from a central spire or dome-like structure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radial Pattern.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Radial pattern**

 
 
• It develops when** streams flow in different directions from a central peak or dome-like structure.**
 
• The radial drainage pattern develops around a central elevated point and is common to conically shaped features such as volcanoes.
 
• When the rivers originate from a hill and flow in all directions, the drainage pattern is known as** ‘radial’.**
 
• E.g. The rivers originating from the **Amarkantak range; Narmada and Son (a tributary of Ganga).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dendritic pattern**

 
 
• This pattern develops where the river channel follows the slope of the terrain.
 
• The stream with its tributaries resembles the branches of a tree, thus the name dendritic. 
 
 
 
• **Trellis pattern**
 
 
• A river joined by its tributaries, at approximately right angles, develops a trellis pattern.
 
• A trellis drainage pattern develops where hard and soft rocks exist parallel to each other. 
 
 
 
• **Rectangular pattern**
 
 
• A rectangular drainage pattern develops on a strongly jointed rocky terrain.

questions.question: Where does the Alaknanda river join the Bhagirathi river in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devprayag **- where **Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers** meet and take the name** Ganga or Ganges River**.
 
• Devprayag (Deva prayāga) is a town and a nagar panchayat (municipality) in Tehri Garhwal district in the state of Uttarakhand, India, and is the final one of the Panch Prayag (five confluences) of Alaknanda River where Alaknanda meets the Bhagirathi river and both rivers thereafter flow on as the Ganges river or Ganga.
 
• "Devprayag" means "Godly Confluence" in Sanskrit.
 
• As per Hindu scriptures, Devprayag is the sacred event of merging two visible heavenly rivers, Alakananda and Bhagirathi, to form the holy Ganga.
 
• Its believed that a third river, the mythical Saraswati river is underground and meets these two rivers at the confluence.
 
• On a terrace in the upper part of the village is the temple of Raghunathji, built of huge stones, pyramidal in form, and capped by a white cupola.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Panch Prayag destinations follow the route created by the Alaknanda river, emerging from Himalaya's Satopanth glacier.
 
• First, Alaknanda meets Dhauliganga river at Vishnuprayag; move on to Nandaprayag to meet Nandakini river then travels to Karnaprayag to join Pindar river.
 
• The River Alaknanda rises at the confluence and is fed of Satopath and Bhagirathi Kharak glacier in Uttarakhand and meets the Sarasvati River tributary at Mana, India, 21 km from Tibet.
 
• Three km below Mana the Alaknanda flows past the Hindu pilgrimage center of Badrinath.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Stanley Reservoir located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stanley Reservoir**__

 __
 
• **Formed by the Mettur Dam in northwestern Tamil Nadu. Hence, Option 1 is correct.**
 
• One of the largest fishing reservoirs in India
 
• Length of the dam – 1700m
 
• Installed capacity of - 240 MW
 
 
 
• **Mettur Dam**__
 
 
• **It is a 1700 m long dam, across the river Cauvery that was constructed in the year 1934. **
 
• **It provides irrigation facilities for 2.75 lakh acres of farmland in parts of Salem, the length of Erode, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruchirappalli, and Thanjavur districts.**
 
• It also serves as a relaxing picnic spot situated 52 Km from Salem. A beautiful park opposite the dam with Lawns, a Children's Play area, and children’s play equipment is an added attraction.
 
• A Hydro Electric and Thermal Power Stations are also located in this town.
 
• It is an industrial center for Aluminum and Chemical products.
 
• **The 75-foot Platinum Jubilee Tower at Mettur Dam serves as a good view tower.**

questions.question: The Deccan plateau lies to the south of which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada. 
 
• The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the north, while the Mahadev, the Kaimur hills and the Maikal range form its eastern extensions.
 
• An extension of the Plateau is also visible in the northeast, locally known as the Meghalaya, Karbi-Anglong Plateau and North Cachar Hills. 
 
• It is separated by a fault from the Chotanagpur Plateau.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers fall into the Arabian Sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tapi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tapti River**__

 __
 
• **The Tapti (also known as the Tapi) is the second-largest west flowing river of Peninsular India and is known as ‘the twin’ or ‘the handmaid’ of the Narmada. Hence, Option 1 is correct.**
 
• **It originates near the Multai reserve forest in Madhya Pradesh** at an elevation of 752 m.
 
• Flows for about 724 km before outfalling into the Arabian Sea through the **Gulf of Cambay [Gulf of Khambhat].**
 
• The Tapti River along with its tributaries flows over the plains of **Vidharbha, Khandesh,** and Gujarat and over large areas in the state of **Maharashtra** and a small area in **Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.**
 
• The basin extends over the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat having an area of ~ 65,000 Sq.km
 
• **Situated in the Deccan plateau**, the basin is **bounded by the Satpura range on the north**, **Mahadev hills on the east, Ajanta Range and the Satmala hills on the south, and by the Arabian Sea on the west.**
 
• The hilly region of the basin is well-forested while the plains are broad and fertile areas suitable for cultivation.
 
• There are two well-defined physical regions, in the basin, viz hilly region and plains; the hilly regions comprising **Satpura, Satmalas, Mahadeo, Ajanta,** and **Gawilgarh hills** are well-forested.
 
• The plain area covers the **Khandesh areas** (Khandesh is a region of central India, which forms the northwestern portion of Maharashtra state) which are broad and fertile, and suitable for cultivation primarily.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f3aaee6a259ff6273312c98a50f5d3578be31485e229343fccda0c790fcda9dc.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Ganges**__

 __
 
• **It is a transboundary river of Asia which flows through India and Bangladesh.**
 
• The 2,525 km river rises in the western Himalayas in the Indian state of Uttarakhand.
 
 
 
• **The Yamuna**__
 __
 
• **Also spelled Jamuna, is the second-largest tributary river of the Ganges by discharge and the longest tributary in India.**
 
 
 
• **The Brahmaputra**__
 
 
• **It is also known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang/Dihang River in Arunachal Pradesh, and Dilao in Assam, is a transboundary river that flows through Tibet, China, India, and Bangladesh.**
 
• It is the 9th largest river in the world by discharge and the 15th longest.

questions.question: In which state is Gobind Sagar (Bhakra Nangal Project) located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Himachal Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gobind Sagar** is a man-made reservoir situated in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• It is part of the **Bhakra Nangal Project**, one of India's largest and most important multipurpose river valley projects.
 
• The reservoir is formed by the **Bhakra Dam**, which is built across the Sutlej River.
 
• The Bhakra Dam is one of the highest gravity dams in the world, with a height of 225.5 meters.
 
• The Gobind Sagar reservoir provides water for irrigation, drinking, and hydroelectric power generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Feature
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Bhakra Dam**
 A concrete gravity dam on the Sutlej River in Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh.
 
 

 **Construction Period**
 The dam was constructed between 1948 and 1963.
 
 

 **Capacity**
 The Gobind Sagar reservoir has a gross storage capacity of about 9.34 billion cubic meters.
 
 

 **Hydroelectric Power**
 The project includes hydroelectric power stations with a total installed capacity of 1,325 MW.
 
 

 **Irrigation**
 Provides irrigation to the states of Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan.
 
 

 **Tourism**
 The Gobind Sagar reservoir is a popular tourist destination, known for its scenic beauty and water sports.

questions.question: Which river flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narmada**:-

 
 
• **The Narmada River flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in central India. (Hence option 1 is correct).**
 
• It is one of the oldest rivers in the world, and is considered to be sacred by Hindus.
 
• The Narmada River flows west for 1,312 kilometers before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Godavari River:-**

 
 
• It originates from Nasik and rises at an elevation of 1,067 m from Trimbakeshwar (Nasik district of Maharashtra), 80 km from the Arabian Sea.
 
• Godavari's total length from its origin to its outfall into the Bay of Bengal is 1,465 km. 
 
 
 
• **Son River:-**
 
 
• It originates from the Amarkantak plateau in the Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh. 
 
• It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, and Jharkhand and finally joins Ganga in Bihar near Patna.
 
• The Bansagar Dam in Madhya Pradesh is also on the Son river.
 
 
 
• **Mahanadi River**
 
 
• It is a river in central India, rising in the hills of southeastern Chhattisgarh state and has a total course of 858 kilometers (533 mi). 
 
• The river originates from Sihawa Mountain in Chhattisgarh.
 
• The largest dam, the Hirakud Dam is built on the river.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the river Brahmaputra is INCORRECT?

options.text: It flows eastwards parallel to the Himalayas.
Most of its courses lies outside India.
It enters India in Arunachal Pradesh where it is called the Dibang.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It enters India in Arunachal Pradesh where it is called the Dibang.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Brahmaputra originates under the name of Siang or Dihang, from the Chemayungdung glacier of the Kailash range near the **Mansarovar lake. Hence, statement 1 is Correct.**
 
• It enters** India west of Sadiya town in Arunachal Pradesh with the name Dihang. *Hence, statement 4 is Incorrect.***
 
• **Tributaries:**
 
 
• Dibang, Lohit, Siang, Burhi Dihing, Tista, and Dhansari.
 
 
 
• It is known as** Tsangpo in Tibet and Yarlung Zangbo in China.**
 
• The river crosses** Assam below Dhubri and enters Bangladesh where the river is known as Jamuna and it flows for 337 km.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Yarlung Tsangpo is the Tibetan name** for the upper course of Brahmaputra.
 
• Most of its course lies outside India.
 
• It flows through countries such as India, China, and Bangladesh.
 
• The Brahmaputra is also called the** "Red River".**
 
• The Brahmaputra is the Indian river that occupies the maximum volume of water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/83ec53be5948da6df4df6fc1ee05f096f4c9eaa4afaf694b601fa0ec1ccfde6d.png]
